sources.entry: Browserdoor - Open-source link picker that asks which browser, browser profile, or Zen space should open each link. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/schowave/browserdoor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar link picker that asks which Zen space, Chrome/Firefox profile, or other browser should open each clicked link.
summary.what_it_does: Browserdoor runs as a menu bar app on macOS 14 or later and acts as the default browser. When a link is clicked in any app, a picker opens at the mouse pointer listing targets: Zen workspaces (read from Zen's session file and opened with the --space flag, Zen 1.24+), each Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi or Chromium profile, each Firefox profile, and other real browsers. Targets can be selected by number key, custom hotkey, arrow keys with Enter, or click. Links arriving at the same moment are grouped so one choice opens them all. Configuration lives in ~/.config/browserdoor/config.json and is re-read each time the picker opens, covering order, hidden targets, labels, hotkeys, default target and extra apps. The README also describes a self-update check and the Homebrew installation path.
use_cases: route links to the right Zen space or client account
choose Chrome or Firefox profile when opening a link
pick which browser opens links from Slack, Mail or Teams
avoid moving tabs between browser profiles by hand
set a macOS default browser that asks each time
notable: Shows each Zen space as its own entry alongside Chrome and Firefox profiles
Reads Chromium Local State and Firefox profiles.ini and profile manager database to list profiles separately
Number keys, custom hotkeys, arrow keys and Enter for fast selection
Groups links that arrive at the same moment into one picker
Config file can be edited by hand or kept in dotfiles
caveats: Zen spaces require Zen 1.24 or later; older versions show as a single entry
Requires macOS 14 or later; on macOS 14 Homebrew builds from source and needs Xcode 16
The update check makes a network request to GitHub (can be turned off)
Upgrading from Doorman or 0.4.x requires re-confirming the default browser and trusting the new formula name
